_source.w: We are learning to practise and apply leadership, collaboration, and group decision-making during physical activities.
y: Leadership and collaboration are essential for success in team settings — and in life.
Practising these skills in physical activity builds our confidence to lead and collaborate in all contexts.
Effective group decision-making leads to better outcomes and more positive experiences for everyone.
eg: Taking a leadership role in organising a team strategy.
Facilitating group decision-making during a game or activity.
Collaborating with teammates to solve a tactical problem.
Providing constructive feedback to peers in a leadership capacity.
Reflecting on our leadership style and its impact on the group.
Evaluating the effectiveness of group decision-making processes during physical activities.

toLevel2.question: What is leadership in physical activity?
toLevel2.correct: Guiding others toward a shared goal in a team or activity
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Leadership guides toward a shared goal.

distractors.answer: Doing every important task yourself so that teammates never need to help out
distractors.explanation: Leadership guides others; it does not mean doing everything alone.

distractors.answer: Following the instructions of others without ever offering any direction at all
distractors.explanation: Leadership offers direction rather than only following.

distractors.answer: Winning personal recognition by outperforming everyone else on the team
distractors.explanation: Leadership serves a shared goal, not personal recognition.

toLevel2.question: What is collaboration?
toLevel2.correct: Working together with others toward a shared outcome in activity

distractors.answer: Competing against your own teammates to prove who is the most capable
distractors.explanation: Collaboration works with teammates, not against them.

distractors.answer: Completing your own part alone without coordinating with anyone else
distractors.explanation: Collaboration involves coordinating, not working in isolation.

distractors.answer: Letting one person make every decision while the rest simply follow
distractors.explanation: Collaboration shares the work and decisions.

toLevel2.question: What is group decision-making?
toLevel2.correct: Choosing together what the team will do in a game or activity

distractors.answer: Letting the coach alone decide everything without any team input at all
distractors.explanation: Group decision-making includes the team, not the coach alone.

distractors.answer: Having each player choose privately and never sharing those choices
distractors.explanation: Group decisions are shared, not made privately.

distractors.answer: Deciding by whoever shouts the loudest rather than by the whole group
distractors.explanation: Group decision-making is collective, not by volume.

toLevel2.question: Who are common formal leaders in sport?
toLevel2.correct: Captains, coaches, and team managers with official roles
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Captains and coaches are formal leaders.

distractors.answer: Spectators and supporters who watch the game from up in the stands
distractors.explanation: Spectators are not formal team leaders.

distractors.answer: Quiet teammates who motivate others without holding any official title
distractors.explanation: Those are informal leaders, not formal ones.

distractors.answer: Opposing players who set the pace of the contest from the other side
distractors.explanation: Opponents are not your team's formal leaders.

toLevel2.question: What is informal leadership?
toLevel2.correct: Leading without an official title, like motivating teammates from the field

distractors.answer: Leading only because you have been given an official captain's title
distractors.explanation: That describes formal leadership, not informal leadership.

distractors.answer: Refusing to take any responsibility unless you are formally in charge
distractors.explanation: Informal leaders take initiative without a title.

distractors.answer: Giving orders that teammates must follow regardless of the situation
distractors.explanation: Informal leadership motivates and supports rather than commands.

toLevel2.question: What is active listening?
toLevel2.correct: Hearing others and responding to what they actually said, not what you assumed

distractors.answer: Hearing the words but replying with whatever you had already planned to say
distractors.explanation: Active listening responds to what was said, not a prepared reply.

distractors.answer: Waiting silently for your turn without taking in what others are saying
distractors.explanation: Active listening involves taking in others' meaning, not just waiting.

distractors.answer: Repeating your own point more loudly until the other person finally agrees
distractors.explanation: Active listening is about understanding, not insisting.

toLevel2.question: What are conflict resolution skills?
toLevel2.correct: Skills that help teams handle disagreement without breaking down

distractors.answer: Skills used to avoid every disagreement by never raising any concerns at all
distractors.explanation: Resolution handles disagreement rather than avoiding all of it.

distractors.answer: Skills for winning every argument so that your own view always prevails
distractors.explanation: Resolution seeks workable outcomes, not winning every argument.

distractors.answer: Skills that matter only for the coach and never for the players themselves
distractors.explanation: Players use conflict-resolution skills too.

toLevel2.question: What is inclusive leadership?
toLevel2.correct: Leadership that makes sure all team members are heard and supported

distractors.answer: Leadership that listens only to the most confident and vocal players present
distractors.explanation: Inclusive leadership hears all members, not only the vocal.

distractors.answer: Leadership that makes every decision alone to save the team a lot of time
distractors.explanation: Inclusive leadership includes others rather than deciding alone.

distractors.answer: Leadership focused on results so that quieter members are simply overlooked
distractors.explanation: Inclusive leadership ensures quieter members are heard.

toLevel2.question: What is role rotation in a team?
toLevel2.correct: Sharing different roles across team members so all build leadership skills

distractors.answer: Keeping the same person in charge so that the team is never disrupted
distractors.explanation: Role rotation shares roles rather than keeping one person in charge.

distractors.answer: Assigning roles by ability so that only the strongest ever lead the team
distractors.explanation: Rotation lets all members build leadership, not only the strongest.

distractors.answer: Rotating only the playing positions while leadership stays with one person
distractors.explanation: Role rotation shares leadership roles, not just positions.

toLevel2.question: What is group consensus?
toLevel2.correct: An agreement everyone in the group can support, even if not first preference

distractors.answer: A decision the majority wins while the minority view is set aside completely
distractors.explanation: Consensus seeks support from all, unlike a pure majority vote.

distractors.answer: A choice made by the leader alone that the group is simply told to accept
distractors.explanation: Consensus is reached together, not imposed by a leader.

distractors.answer: An outcome that satisfies only the players with the strongest opinions
distractors.explanation: Consensus is something the whole group can support.

toLevel2.question: What is voting in group decisions?
toLevel2.correct: A way of deciding by counting individual preferences fairly

distractors.answer: A way of deciding by letting the captain choose on behalf of everyone
distractors.explanation: Voting counts individual preferences rather than one person choosing.

distractors.answer: A way of avoiding any decision until absolutely everyone fully agrees
distractors.explanation: That describes consensus-seeking, not voting.

distractors.answer: A way of deciding based only on who argues the most forcefully
distractors.explanation: Voting counts preferences fairly, not by force of argument.

toLevel2.question: How does First Nations leadership often value community?
toLevel2.correct: It centres collective responsibility, Country, and intergenerational decision-making

distractors.answer: It focuses on one individual making decisions for personal recognition
distractors.explanation: First Nations leadership often centres community, not the individual.

distractors.answer: It values quick decisions made without consulting the wider community
distractors.explanation: It values collective, intergenerational decision-making.

distractors.answer: It separates leadership from any connection to Country or community
distractors.explanation: Connection to Country and community is central to it.

toLevel3.question: Why does leadership matter in team activity?
toLevel3.correct: Without leadership, teams can lose direction and miss shared goals

distractors.answer: With leadership, teams always win regardless of their effort or skill
distractors.explanation: Leadership helps direction; it does not guarantee winning.

distractors.answer: Leadership matters only to the coach and not to the players themselves
distractors.explanation: Leadership matters to players too.

distractors.answer: Teams perform best when no one ever takes any direction at all
distractors.explanation: Some direction helps teams stay on track.

toLevel3.question: Why is collaboration central to team play?
toLevel3.correct: Working together is what turns a group of individuals into a team

distractors.answer: Working separately is what lets each player perform at their personal best
distractors.explanation: Collaboration, not working separately, builds a team.

distractors.answer: A group becomes a team only when one strong leader takes full control
distractors.explanation: Teams form through collaboration, not one person's control.

distractors.answer: Collaboration mainly slows a team down compared with individual effort
distractors.explanation: Collaboration is what makes a team more than individuals.

toLevel3.question: Why does group decision-making strengthen teams?
toLevel3.correct: Decisions made together are more likely to be accepted and acted on

distractors.answer: Decisions made by one person alone are always accepted faster by the team
distractors.explanation: Shared decisions gain more buy-in than solo ones.

distractors.answer: Decisions made together mainly waste time without improving team buy-in
distractors.explanation: Shared decisions improve acceptance and follow-through.

distractors.answer: Decisions are best kept secret so that players cannot question them
distractors.explanation: Open, shared decisions are more likely to be acted on.

toLevel3.question: Why are both formal and informal leaders important?
toLevel3.correct: Formal roles guide the group; informal leaders motivate, support, and connect

distractors.answer: Formal roles are all that matter, since informal leaders add little value
distractors.explanation: Both formal and informal leaders matter.

distractors.answer: Informal leaders should replace captains so that no official roles are needed
distractors.explanation: Both kinds of leader play a part; one need not replace the other.

distractors.answer: Only one type of leader can ever help a team at any given time
distractors.explanation: Formal and informal leaders both help, together.

toLevel3.question: Why is active listening more than just hearing?
toLevel3.correct: It involves responding to what was actually said, not what you assumed
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Active listening responds to what was said.

distractors.answer: It involves nodding along while planning your own reply in your head
distractors.explanation: Active listening responds to the actual message, not a planned reply.

distractors.answer: It simply means staying quiet until the other person finally stops talking
distractors.explanation: Active listening is more than waiting silently.

distractors.answer: It means hearing the words without needing to respond to them at all
distractors.explanation: Active listening includes responding to what was said.

toLevel3.question: Why are conflict resolution skills crucial in teams?
toLevel3.correct: Disagreement is normal, and good resolution stops it from breaking the team down

distractors.answer: Disagreement should never happen, so resolution skills are rarely ever needed
distractors.explanation: Disagreement is normal; resolution skills are valuable.

distractors.answer: Disagreement is best ignored so that the team can simply move on quickly
distractors.explanation: Resolution addresses disagreement rather than ignoring it.

distractors.answer: Resolution matters only when the coach steps in to settle every dispute
distractors.explanation: Teams resolve conflict themselves, not only via the coach.

toLevel3.question: Why is inclusive leadership especially important in school PE?
toLevel3.correct: It makes sure all students are heard and supported, not just the loudest

distractors.answer: It focuses attention on the loudest students so lessons keep moving quickly
distractors.explanation: Inclusive leadership hears all students, not just the loudest.

distractors.answer: It matters only in elite sport rather than in everyday classroom PE lessons
distractors.explanation: Inclusive leadership is important in school PE.

distractors.answer: It leaves quieter students to catch up on their own without any support
distractors.explanation: Inclusive leadership supports quieter students too.

toLevel3.question: Why does role rotation build shared leadership?
toLevel3.correct: Sharing different roles lets all team members build leadership skills over time

distractors.answer: Keeping one captain in every game builds the strongest leadership over time
distractors.explanation: Sharing roles, not fixing one captain, builds wider leadership.

distractors.answer: Sharing roles mainly confuses the team and slows down their development
distractors.explanation: Role sharing builds skills across the team.

distractors.answer: Only naturally talented players can ever build leadership skills in a team
distractors.explanation: All members can build leadership through shared roles.

toLevel3.question: Why is consensus often better than majority vote?
toLevel3.correct: Consensus builds shared agreement even with minority views, not just majority wins

distractors.answer: Consensus simply lets the majority overrule the minority more quickly
distractors.explanation: Consensus seeks agreement including minority views.

distractors.answer: A majority vote always builds stronger agreement than seeking consensus
distractors.explanation: Consensus can build broader shared agreement than a vote.

distractors.answer: Consensus means the leader decides after briefly hearing everyone out
distractors.explanation: Consensus is shared agreement, not a leader's decision.

toLevel3.question: Why is voting still useful sometimes?
toLevel3.correct: Voting gives a fair, quick way to decide when consensus cannot be reached

distractors.answer: Voting should always replace consensus because counting is simpler and faster
distractors.explanation: Voting is useful when consensus fails, not a blanket replacement.

distractors.answer: Voting is unfair because it ignores the preferences of individual players
distractors.explanation: Voting counts individual preferences fairly.

distractors.answer: Voting works only when every single member already agrees on the choice
distractors.explanation: Voting is precisely for when full agreement is not reached.

toLevel3.question: Why do cultural protocols shape leadership in many teams?
toLevel3.correct: Different cultures bring different leadership traditions that shape how teams work

distractors.answer: All cultures share exactly one leadership style, so traditions never differ
distractors.explanation: Leadership traditions differ across cultures.

distractors.answer: Cultural background has no effect on how a team chooses to lead itself
distractors.explanation: Cultural traditions do shape team leadership.

distractors.answer: Only the coach's culture matters when deciding how a team is led
distractors.explanation: Many members' cultural traditions shape how teams work.

distractors.answer: It values quick decisions made without consulting the wider community
distractors.explanation: It values collective, intergenerational decision-making.

distractors.answer: It separates leadership from any connection to Country or community
distractors.explanation: Connection to Country and community is central to it.

toLevel5.question: Evaluate: how do leadership and collaboration support PE teams?

distractors.answer: Individual talent alone, without collaboration, is what builds the strongest teams
distractors.explanation: Teams are built on leadership and collaboration, not talent alone.

distractors.answer: Strict instructions from one leader are all a strong team really needs
distractors.explanation: Strong teams also need collaboration and shared decisions.

distractors.answer: Strong teams depend only on fitness, not on leadership or decision-making
distractors.explanation: Leadership and decision-making matter alongside fitness.

toLevel5.question: Justify: why does leadership matter in team activity?
toLevel5.correct: Without leadership, teams can lose direction and miss shared goals

distractors.answer: With leadership, teams always win regardless of their effort or skill
distractors.explanation: Leadership helps direction; it does not guarantee winning.

distractors.answer: Leadership matters only to the coach and not to the players themselves
distractors.explanation: Leadership matters to players too.

distractors.answer: Teams perform best when no one ever takes any direction at all
distractors.explanation: Some direction helps teams stay on track.

toLevel5.question: Assess: when does collaboration most turn a group into a team?
toLevel5.correct: When working together becomes more important than individual results

distractors.answer: When each player focuses only on their own personal statistics and results
distractors.explanation: Teamwork forms when shared effort outweighs individual results.

distractors.answer: When one talented individual carries the group without needing the others
distractors.explanation: A team forms through collaboration, not one carrying the rest.

distractors.answer: When the team avoids working together to keep things simple and fast
distractors.explanation: Working together is what makes a group a team.

toLevel5.question: Critique: a risk of leadership without listening is what?
toLevel5.correct: It can push past quieter voices and miss key information from the team

distractors.answer: It speeds up decisions so much that the team always reaches the best outcome
distractors.explanation: Skipping listening can miss key input, not guarantee the best outcome.

distractors.answer: It mainly affects the leader's own confidence rather than the wider team
distractors.explanation: It affects the whole team by missing information.

distractors.answer: It improves team unity by making sure only one clear voice is ever heard
distractors.explanation: Hearing only one voice can miss important team information.

toLevel5.question: Evaluate: how do formal and informal leaders complement each other?
toLevel5.correct: Formal roles guide the group; informal leaders motivate, support, and connect

distractors.answer: Formal roles are all that matter, since informal leaders add little value
distractors.explanation: Both formal and informal leaders matter.

distractors.answer: Informal leaders should replace captains so that no official roles are needed
distractors.explanation: Both kinds of leader play a part; one need not replace the other.

distractors.answer: Only one type of leader can ever help a team at any given time
distractors.explanation: Formal and informal leaders both help, together.

toLevel5.question: Justify: why are conflict resolution skills crucial?
toLevel5.correct: Disagreement is normal, and good resolution stops it from breaking the team down

distractors.answer: Disagreement should never happen, so resolution skills are rarely ever needed
distractors.explanation: Disagreement is normal; resolution skills are valuable.

distractors.answer: Disagreement is best ignored so that the team can simply move on quickly
distractors.explanation: Resolution addresses disagreement rather than ignoring it.

distractors.answer: Resolution matters only when the coach steps in to settle every dispute
distractors.explanation: Teams resolve conflict themselves, not only via the coach.

toLevel5.question: Assess: when does inclusive leadership most matter?
toLevel5.correct: When quiet or new team members would otherwise not be heard

distractors.answer: When the most confident players need even more chances to speak up
distractors.explanation: Inclusive leadership matters most for those not otherwise heard.

distractors.answer: When the team is already winning and needs no further input at all
distractors.explanation: Inclusion matters regardless of the score.

distractors.answer: When only the coach's voice should be heard during a close game
distractors.explanation: Inclusive leadership brings in quiet and new members.

toLevel5.question: Critique: a risk of always letting the same person lead is what?
toLevel5.correct: Without role rotation, others miss the chance to build leadership skills
toLevel5.correctExplanation: Same leader every time blocks growth.

distractors.answer: With role rotation, the team loses all stability and cannot perform well
distractors.explanation: Rotation builds skills while teams can still perform.

distractors.answer: Keeping one leader is best because rotation only confuses the players
distractors.explanation: Rotation gives more members the chance to lead.

distractors.answer: Leadership skills are fixed at birth, so rotation cannot build them anyway
distractors.explanation: Leadership skills can be built through practice and rotation.

distractors.answer: Consensus means the leader decides after briefly hearing everyone out

distractors.explanation: Voting counts individual preferences fairly.

distractors.answer: Voting works only when every single member already agrees on the choice

distractors.explanation: Protocols shape teams by respecting different traditions.

distractors.answer: When only the captain's cultural tradition is allowed to shape the team
distractors.explanation: Many traditions can shape a team side by side.

toLevel5.correct: Different teams and contexts need different leadership styles to work well
toLevel5.correctExplanation: One style does not fit all.

distractors.answer: One single leadership style works equally well for every team and situation
distractors.explanation: Different contexts call for different leadership styles.

distractors.answer: Leadership style never affects how well a team actually performs together
distractors.explanation: Leadership style does affect team performance.

distractors.answer: Only the strictest leadership style ever works across all teams and contexts
distractors.explanation: No single style fits every team and context.
